scenes.title: One electron, two slits
scenes.say: Fire one electron at a wall with two slits. Where does it land? Today we go find out. In the *quantum realm.*

scenes.title: Lumen: set destination
scenes.say: First, the Lumen. Scale: {10⁻¹⁰ meters|ten to the minus ten meters}. Atomic. Ahh, *here we go.*

scenes.title: The double-slit experiment
scenes.say: Electrons go through one at a time. Each one lands as a single dot. Random. *Unpredictable.*
scenes.source: Animated with the two-slit interference pattern; dots are sampled, not a recording

scenes.title: Then stripes appear
scenes.say: But after thousands of dots, stripes appear. An *interference* pattern. Each electron's wave goes through both slits and interferes with itself.
scenes.source: Animated with the two-slit interference pattern; dots are sampled, not a recording

scenes.title: Watch it, and it changes
scenes.say: Now measure which slit each electron used. The stripes *vanish.* Two plain bands. Observing the path destroys the interference.

scenes.title: This really happened

items: A Hitachi team filmed single electrons building the stripes, one dot at a time
The same experiment works with atoms and even large molecules

scenes.say: This isn't theory. In {1989|nineteen eighty-nine}, a Hitachi team filmed single electrons building these stripes, *one dot at a time.*
scenes.source: Tonomura et al., American Journal of Physics 57, 117 (1989)

scenes.title: Lumen: home
scenes.say: That's enough weirdness for one day. *Lumen,* take us home.

scenes.say: Class dismissed. Go build something. Stop waiting for that *interview.*
